title: Add Two Numbers
description: Two singly-linked lists store digits in reverse order. Walk both with a carry; build the sum list using a dummy head. Continue while either list has nodes left or carry is non-zero.

notes: Lists store digits in reverse order — the head is the ones place. That means you add left-to-right without any reversal step.
Loop condition is `l1 || l2 || carry` — a leftover carry creates a new most-significant digit (e.g. 5 + 5 → [0, 1]).
Use a dummy head so you don't special-case the first appended node.
Read each list's val defensively (0 if null) since the two lists can differ in length.

questions.q: Why is the loop condition `l1 || l2 || carry`?
options: A leftover carry can produce one more digit even after both lists run out

questions.q: Which digit does the HEAD of each list represent?
What does the dummy head simplify?
options: It avoids a special case when appending the first sum node

questions.q: Time complexity for lists of length m and n?

exercises.prompt: Fill in carry-propagating addition over two reversed-digit lists.

blanks.hint: leftover carry needs one more digit
first real node sits after the dummy

L3.prompt: Write `addTwoNumbers(l1, l2)` where each list represents a non-negative integer with digits stored in reverse. Return the sum as a list. Use toList/toArr helpers. Log `JSON.stringify(toArr(addTwoNumbers(toList([2, 4, 3]), toList([5, 6, 4]))))`.
hints: Walk both lists with a carry; loop while either list or the carry is non-zero.
Treat a missing node as 0 so unequal lengths just work.
Use a dummy head; append `{ val: sum % 10, next: null }` and advance the tail.
